long_biography.plain_text:
At the University of Michigan, Evans reported from Washington after President Kennedy's assassination and later ran the campus radio station. Drafted during the Vietnam War, he became a Navy television and public-affairs officer aboard USS America. In 1976 he took responsibility for financing and building Arlington's cable system, creating a showcase for the emerging industry near Washington.

As president of Hauser Communications, Evans helped expand a regional cable portfolio whose systems were sold in the 1990s. He also gave C-SPAN technical and logistical support from its earliest meetings, then served for decades on its board. His foundation later funded AIDS-vaccine research, higher education, digital preservation and LGBTQ+ human-rights programmes.
